cases.setup_script:
: > "$HOME/control.txt"
kat=$(printf %s password | /usr/bin/argon2 somesalt -id -t 2 -k 65536 -p 1 -l 32 -r)
[[ $kat == 09316115d5cf24ed5a15a31a3ba326e5cf32edc24702987c02b6566f61913cf7 ]]
enc=$(printf %s password | /usr/bin/argon2 somesalt -id -t 2 -k 65536 -p 1 -l 32 -e)
[[ $enc == '$argon2id$v=19$m=65536,t=2,p=1$c29tZXNhbHQ$CTFhFdXPJO1aFaMaO6Mm5c8y7cJHAph8ArZWb2GRPPc' ]]
printf 'argon2: reference vector password/somesalt t=2 m=65536 p=1 raw and encoded match\n' >> "$HOME/control.txt"
[[ $(/usr/bin/python3 -I phc.py oracle "$enc" kat.pw) == kdf=match ]]
[[ $(/usr/bin/python3 -I phc.py oracle '$argon2id$v=19$m=65536,t=2,p=1$736f6d6573616c74$09316115d5cf24ed5a15a31a3ba326e5cf32edc24702987c02b6566f61913cf7' kat.pw) == kdf=match ]]
printf 'phc.py: reference vector recomputed from the B64 and hex layouts\n' >> "$HOME/control.txt"
cases.purpose: set-fd writes an Argon2id PHC string in the standard encoding with the configured parameters (PHCLIB_M/T/P, and the documented defaults when unset), a 16-byte salt and a 32-byte hash whose value the independent argon2 CLI recomputes from the stored salt and the password; a second set uses a fresh salt; the last-change day becomes today while the other aging fields stay; other rows, the shadow mode and the directory stay clean; the password appears in no database or diagnostic file. Encoding, parameters and the recomputed key are separate lines so an encoding divergence does not hide the key check.
cases.oracle: Argon2id per RFC 9106 computed by the independent argon2 CLI (phc-winner-argon2 20190702, /usr/bin/argon2) in the guest; the PHC string format (password-hashing competition 'PHC string format': $argon2id$v=19$m=M,t=T,p=P$<salt>$<hash> with salt and hash in unpadded standard B64, as argon2 -e and libargon2 produce); passwd(1)/shadow(5): changing a password sets the last-change day and keeps the other aging fields, the account must exist, and the database is unchanged on refusal. Parameters: PHCLIB_M/PHCLIB_T/PHCLIB_P and the documented defaults m=19456, t=2, p=1 (passwd.c header; RFC 9106 second recommended set). A trailing newline ends the password read from the descriptor (chpasswd/--stdin convention). setup_script runs the CLI on the reference test vector before anything else.
cases.comparison: Exact lines: status, encoding class, parameters and byte lengths, CLI recomputation result, aging fields, other rows, mode, residue, salt freshness and the secret search.
cases.script:
[[ $(type -t passwd) == builtin ]] || { printf 'candidate passwd builtin missing\n'; exit 99; }
export BASHPASSWD_KERNEL_SECRETS=0 PHCLIB_PASSWD=db/passwd PHCLIB_SHADOW=db/shadow PHCLIB_GROUP=db/group PHCLIB_M=1024 PHCLIB_T=1 PHCLIB_P=1
reset_db() { /usr/bin/rm -rf db; /usr/bin/mkdir db; /usr/bin/cp pristine/passwd pristine/group pristine/shadow db/; /usr/bin/chmod 600 db/shadow; }
snap() { /usr/bin/rm -rf snap; /usr/bin/cp -a db snap; }
same() { /usr/bin/cmp -s db/passwd snap/passwd && /usr/bin/cmp -s db/group snap/group && /usr/bin/cmp -s db/shadow snap/shadow && echo unchanged || echo changed; }
residue() { local n=0 f; for f in "$1"/* "$1"/.[!.]*; do [[ -e $f ]] || continue; case ${f##*/} in passwd|group|shadow) ;; *) n=$((n + 1)) ;; esac; done; echo "$n"; }
rc_class() { (( $1 == 0 )) && echo 0 || echo nonzero; }
today=$(( $(printf '%(%s)T' -1) / 86400 ))
phc() { /usr/bin/python3 -I phc.py "$@"; }
reset_db
row() { /usr/bin/awk -F: -v u="$1" '$1 == u { print $2 }' db/shadow; }
setpw() {  # USER LABEL: set-fd from pw; repeat (at most 8 times) while the random salt holds a NUL byte the CLI cannot take
  local i rc
  for i in 1 2 3 4 5 6 7 8; do
    passwd set-fd "$1" 3 3< pw 2>> "$HOME/err.$2"; rc=$?
    (( rc == 0 )) || return "$rc"
    [[ $(phc oracle "$(row "$1")" pw.raw) == kdf=salt-nul ]] || return 0
  done
}
report() {  # LABEL RC USER
  local r; r=$(row "$3")
  printf '%s rc=%d\n' "$1" "$2"
  phc info "$r"
  phc oracle "$r" pw.raw
}
setpw carol set; report set "$?" carol
/usr/bin/awk -F: -v t="$today" '$1 == "carol" { printf "aging=[%s:%s:%s:%s:%s:%s:%s]\n", ($3 == t ? "today" : $3), $4, $5, $6, $7, $8, $9 }' db/shadow
/usr/bin/grep -v '^carol:' db/shadow | /usr/bin/cmp -s - <(/usr/bin/grep -v '^carol:' pristine/shadow) && o=unchanged || o=changed
printf 'other-rows=%s shadow-other=%s residue=%s\n' "$o" "$(( 8#$(/usr/bin/stat -c %a db/shadow) & 7 ))" "$(residue db)"
s1=$(phc salt "$(row carol)")
setpw carol again; rc=$?
printf 'again rc=%d %s salt-fresh=%s\n' "$rc" "$(phc oracle "$(row carol)" pw.raw)" "$([[ $(phc salt "$(row carol)") != "$s1" ]] && echo yes || echo no)"
( export PHCLIB_M=2048 PHCLIB_T=3 PHCLIB_P=2; setpw alice params ); report params "$?" alice
( unset PHCLIB_M PHCLIB_T PHCLIB_P; setpw alice defaults ); report defaults "$?" alice
leak=none
for f in db/* "$HOME"/err.*; do /usr/bin/grep -qF synthetic-pass-1 "$f" && leak=${f##*/}; done
printf 'secret-in-files=%s\n' "$leak"
/usr/bin/rm -rf db snap
cases.stdout:
set rc=0
format=b64
params=m=1024,t=1,p=1 salt-bytes=16 hash-bytes=32
kdf=match
aging=[today:1:90:14:30:20000:]
other-rows=unchanged shadow-other=0 residue=0
again rc=0 kdf=match salt-fresh=yes
params rc=0
format=b64
params=m=2048,t=3,p=2 salt-bytes=16 hash-bytes=32
kdf=match
defaults rc=0
format=b64
params=m=19456,t=2,p=1 salt-bytes=16 hash-bytes=32
kdf=match
secret-in-files=none

cases.purpose: set-fd refuses an empty password, an unreadable descriptor, an account that is not in the passwd database, an invalid name, and BASHPASSWD_REQUIRE_KERNEL_SECRETS=1 while /dev/bashos-auth is absent, each without changing any database file or leaving temporary files; missing operands are usage errors.
cases.oracle: Argon2id per RFC 9106 computed by the independent argon2 CLI (phc-winner-argon2 20190702, /usr/bin/argon2) in the guest; the PHC string format (password-hashing competition 'PHC string format': $argon2id$v=19$m=M,t=T,p=P$<salt>$<hash> with salt and hash in unpadded standard B64, as argon2 -e and libargon2 produce); passwd(1)/shadow(5): changing a password sets the last-change day and keeps the other aging fields, the account must exist, and the database is unchanged on refusal. Parameters: PHCLIB_M/PHCLIB_T/PHCLIB_P and the documented defaults m=19456, t=2, p=1 (passwd.c header; RFC 9106 second recommended set). A trailing newline ends the password read from the descriptor (chpasswd/--stdin convention). setup_script runs the CLI on the reference test vector before anything else. The kernel-secret requirement must fail closed when the device is absent (the device-backed path itself stays an open capability gap); setup_script proves the device is absent.
